_note: Where xUnit and Fitness are recorded as disagreeing, read by harness.py. D1-D12 are the 12 disagreements SL-022 recorded, as strict rows: a row that both engines now agree on fails as DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, and the fix is to delete it here and its D-id in the divergence list of the .taad/fitness.yaml header, in the same change. D1-D5 come from SL-022's divergence run (packages/, dist/, the two case-only renames, the using split across two lines), D6-D7 from its encoding run (UTF-16LE, over 2 MB), and D8-D12 from the divergence tree of its final validation (target/, TestNative.cs to Testnative.cs, over 2 MB with an interop line, UTF-16LE under tests/, a blank line before a using). That tree's split using is the D5 shape and is not repeated. D12 differs only in the line each engine reports, so it records the planted-line offset each engine fired at. D13 was measured by SL-031, not SL-022, and is not a divergence: a single-byte cp1252 file is read as UTF-8 with replacement by both engines, so an ASCII violation in it fires in both. It pins that, so the header's 'not UTF-8' line cannot be read as covering it. Outcomes are changed by hand only.

rows.note: Fitness skips a folder named packages/ at any depth; xUnit skips only bin/ and obj/.
Fitness skips a folder named dist/ at any depth.
xUnit's .Except([...]) compares case-sensitively and Fitness's except_files do not, so the exempted classifier's own reparse check fires in xUnit only.
Fitness matches the whole file, so \s+ crosses the line break; xUnit matches one line at a time. The pattern text is the same in both copies.
Fitness decodes every file as UTF-8; xUnit decodes by the byte-order mark.
Fitness does not read a file over 2,000,000 bytes.
Fitness skips a folder named target/ at any depth.
Both fire, at different lines: Fitness reports a (?m)^\s* match at the blank line before the using (offset 1), xUnit at the using (offset 2).
